proposals.title: Replay lens health on past dates from the scan's dated readings
proposals.outcome: A history reader who travels to a past week sees which features were bad or watch under each lens on that date. The plan shows trouble marks and flags; the feature page shows health, the matching rule's reason and the readings it was judged on. The timeline hairline marks weeks where health moved ('3 went bad · 2 cleared'). This holds wherever the stored readings cover every field the lens rules read; everywhere else the page still says 'Not recorded for that date'.
proposals.builds_on: Honest time: one presenter (lensAsOf / recordAsOf) is the only home of the as-of rule, and LiveFacets already works out health from readings with the standard evaluator instead of trusting stored health.
proposals.mechanism: Add a pure core healthAsOf(f, def, scan, t). It takes the map's facet, lays over each metric's last reading on or before t (metricHistory, with the same rules as LiveFacets.take), binds stage-bound fields to stageAt(f, t), then runs readLens / evaluateLens. A pair can be replayed only when every field named by the lens's usable rules and applies_when (conditionFields) is either a metric with a reading by t or stage-bound. Otherwise it stays 'none' as today. Where the events log has lens-health events (the format defines them), they are a second source for pairs without metrics. lensAsOf gains an at:'replayed' result carrying health, why and a label: 'replayed by today's rules (manifest v…), from N readings up to <date>'. The engine computes the replay once per (travelled date, scan revision) as a lookup table. The trouble-mark check in plan.ts (`st && now`) and the off-now early return in layoutFlags read that table, so marks and flags draw on past dates while the fill stays the stage. weekChanges adds health moves from the same replay. No schema change.
proposals.evidence: Observed: LiveFacets.evaluate already reads lens health from readings through readLens, so replay is that evaluator plus a date filter. Measurements are append-only with measured_at and indexed by (feature, lens, metric, measured_at). valueView already finds the last reading on or before t for one field. The dossier lists the gap ('health has no history although the event log defines lens-health'). Prior art: Prometheus promtool backfills recording rules over stored history, i.e. today's rules over yesterday's data, and only from when data exists (https://mankier.com/1/promtool). Hypothesis: the share of replayable pairs depends on how many lenses' rules read only metric fields. Kettle has one point per metric and gains little until its sample gets dated readings; the value is on live products with two or more runs.
proposals.risk: Today's rules over old readings could be mistaken for what the page said back then. Mitigation: label every replayed value with the manifest version and reading count; replay only pairs whose inputs are fully covered; extend check:timeview so a pair that reads a non-metric field still returns Not recorded. Cost: about features × lenses evaluations per travelled date, computed on the discrete date change and never per frame.
proposals.verify: New check:timeview cases on a fixture: a metric reads 120 on 10-01 and 60 on 10-20 against the rule 'gt 100 -> bad'. At t=10-10 the presenter returns replayed bad with the rule's reason; at t=10-25 it returns good; a lens whose rule reads an enum facet field returns Not recorded on both dates. On a live product with two or more runs, flags drawn at a past week go from 0 (layoutFlags returns none off-now) to the replayed count, and the hairline shows health-move marks. perf.py: gesture p50 stays at or under 16.7 ms at ?scale=4 on a travelled date.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: The timeline stops being a stage-only replay. It answers 'when did this go bad, and what cleared it', which is the question a history reader brings, without ever showing a current value for a past date.

proposals.title: Announce every keyboard move with the place's own lens summary
proposals.outcome: A keyboard or screen-reader user who walks rooms (left/right), zooms (+/-) or switches lens (digits) hears a summary such as 'Room Payments · wing B · 12 features · 3 in trouble under Security: 2 secrets found · 2 questions wait'. It is built from the same lens aggregates the plan's labels draw. At bay and room level, Tab from the canvas reaches that place's features one by one with their health word, and Enter opens one.
proposals.builds_on: Every lens, including custom manifest lenses, already supplies a code-free place aggregate (ChannelAggregate.parts and trouble), and the hover card already turns it into a place summary for mouse users.
proposals.mechanism: Move HoverBody's place summary into a pure placeWords(E, place, view, t) and reuse it in the hover card. Add a visually hidden polite live region that subscribes to store.place, view and t. syncPlace only writes place when the camera's place really changes, so the region gets one update per arrival. The text is replaced, not appended, and it waits for the same 600 ms rest that browser history already uses, so a fly-through stays quiet. At room and bay level, a roving-tabindex list of DOM proxies for the visible tiles gives Tab and arrow access with HWORD health words. The canvas's long aria-label becomes a short name plus a pointer to the live region. No frame-loop work: React reads only on discrete store changes.
proposals.evidence: Observed: the recorded standards verdict is exactly this gap (canvas-graph/canvas-accessibility deviation: walk() only flies the camera, so a keyboard walk announces nothing). No component announces place changes: the only aria-live regions under apps/web/src/components are in the companion, crossing, focus and ledger panels. syncPlace already turns camera movement into discrete place records in the store. Prior art: ApexCharts maps replace a polite region's text on each arrow key and use a roving tabindex with a feature-count limit (https://apexcharts.com/apexmaps/docs/accessibility/); Esri recommends a hidden polite region for map state (https://www.esri.com/arcgis-blog/products/js-api-arcgis/developers/build-accessibility-into-your-web-maps-with-arcgis-maps-sdk-for-javascript).
proposals.risk: Too many announcements during flights or rapid walks. Mitigation: announce only once the place has rested, replace the text instead of queueing, and announce lens and date changes only when they change the sentence. The tile-proxy list could get large at room level; cap it per bay as ApexCharts does and fall back to the room sentence above the cap.
proposals.verify: A node check (check:place-words) asserts the sentence for three places under General, one built-in lens and the code-free com.kettle.cost lens. A browser run shows that pressing ArrowRight twice changes the live region's text exactly twice, and Tab from the canvas focuses a tile proxy whose name carries its health word. A lens-scan re-judge moves canvas-graph/canvas-accessibility from deviation to conformant and blueprint-canvas a11y off 'partial'.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Every lens anyone adds becomes audible with no extra code, so the promise that the plan is readable at any zoom holds for people who don't use sight or a mouse.

proposals.title: Tie each 'what clears it' step to the proposal that would clear it
proposals.outcome: On a lens tab, each verified step says whether a proposal already targets it (same feature, lens and metric) and whether that proposal's expected change would actually clear the rule, e.g. 'P-41 approved: 420 → 340 ms, clears BAD' or 'falls 20 ms short'. Once the proposal is built it shows what was delivered ('measured 310 after: cleared'). A step with no proposal offers 'Propose a fix for this step', which queues a propose job for that feature, lens and target.
proposals.builds_on: clearPath's verified steps (every target applied and the rules re-run), plus the scan-finding contract that every proposal names a metric and an expected delta.
proposals.mechanism: Add a pure coverStep(step, proposals, values, manifest). It matches proposals by baseId(feature) + lens + metric == step.field, with status proposed, approved, executing or done. It applies now + expected_delta (the arithmetic Queue.metricMove already does) and re-runs the step's rule with evaluateCondition, the same way clearPath verifies, giving clears / short by X / makes it worse. For done items with after_value it gives the delivered verdict. ClearSteps shows one chip per step that links to the existing Approve/Decline in SwarmSection and to the answer track. For uncovered steps, a propose job scoped to one feature (ScanScope kind 'feature' already exists) carries a target hint (field, op, value) to /lens-scan propose. That route stays localhost-only behind BP_WRITES, and Kettle's scan sim answers the same way.
proposals.evidence: Observed: clearPath is used only by General.tsx:26 and LensPanel.tsx:140 and never looks at proposals. Proposal carries metric and expected_delta in metric units (Queue.tsx computes last.value + d). A 'propose' job kind exists but is queued only across all lenses and all features (enqueueAllLenses). Hypothesis: many proposals' expected deltas are written without reference to the rule's threshold, and the 'short by' verdict will show which ones.
proposals.risk: The propose button needs the lens-scan skill to accept a feature scope and a target, which is a skill change, not just UI. Mitigation: ship the read side first (coverage chips, a pure function with its own check); it is useful on its own. A proposal can name the metric while aiming at a different rule; the verdict is computed against this step's rule only, so it never over-claims.
proposals.verify: check:clear-cover fixture: a step latency 420 → at most 400. Proposal A (−80) → clears; B (−10) → short by 10; C (done, after_value 390) → delivered, cleared; no match → uncovered. On Kettle: count the uncovered steps on one lens's bad features; after 'Propose a fix', a new proposal row appears with metric = step.field and that chip turns to covered on the next scan delta.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: 'What clears it' goes from advice to a ledger: for every red reading the page says whether someone is already fixing it and whether that fix is big enough.

proposals.title: Punch list: the plan computes the verified route to done for any milestone
proposals.outcome: Pick any milestone in the map (not only the sample's payments-ga), or a selected target or place, and the plan becomes its punch list. Everything outside it dims. Each room's label says '5 steps · 1 blocked', and flags inside are numbered in walk order. A callout lists every verified step grouped by room, marked covered or uncovered by a proposal. J/K walk the steps with the camera. The headline reads, for example, 'Payments GA: 23 of 31 features clear every lens; 14 steps left, 6 covered by proposals that would clear them, 3 blocked'. Live products get a readiness view for the first time.
proposals.builds_on: GA readiness mode (dimming, framing, the callout) and clearPath, which today works for one feature under one lens at a time.
proposals.mechanism: Add a pure core punchList(P, scope). For each feature in scope and each enabled lens reading watch or bad, it runs clearPath to get steps or a blocked reason. A cross-lens pass then applies all of a feature's steps and re-evaluates every lens, marking 'conflicts with <lens>'. Features are ordered by remaining effort (step count, then relative distance |target−now|/|now|); rooms follow M.L.walk. Per-place counts are cached like lensAgg and invalidated on healthV. Generalize S.ga to S.punch = {milestone | target}. syncModeFilters' dimFn becomes 'in scope', setMode frames tilesBox, the GA callout serves any P.milestones entry, G opens a picker when there is more than one milestone, and the hash carries punch=<id>. Drawing adds counts to room labels and numbers to existing flags only: no new tile colours. Each step links to its lens tab at 'what clears it', and coverage comes from coverStep when it exists.
proposals.evidence: Observed: GA mode is tied to GA_MILESTONE = 'payments-ga' and counts only stage, blockers and live-but-bad features (Overlays.tsx:401-402). hasGA is false on a live product, so the mode, its key and its overlay don't exist there (Engine.ts:777-778), even though v3 maps carry milestones (load.ts reads them). clearPath already verifies each step by applying targets and re-running the rules, so a punch list is a deterministic fold over it, with no model call. Prior art: construction punch lists pin each open item to its spot on the drawing, with open and closed shown by pin state (https://support.procore.com/products/online/user-guide/project-level/drawings/tutorials/pinning-and-connected-items-in-the-drawings-tool-open-beta). Hypothesis, not measured: owners will open it before every milestone.
proposals.risk: Steps under different lenses can conflict (fixing cost may raise latency), and clearPath verifies one lens at a time. Mitigation: the cross-lens pass above, with conflicts said in words rather than hidden. Clutter at site zoom: numbers ride on existing flags and counts on existing labels, nothing recolours a node. Cost: the list is computed on discrete changes only; perf budgets must hold with the mode on.
proposals.verify: check:punch fixture: a milestone with 4 features (one clean, one with 1 step, one with 3 steps, one blocked) yields '1 of 4 clear every lens, 4 steps, 1 blocked'; J visits rooms in M.L.walk order; a cross-lens conflict is reported. With ?product= on a live map that has a milestone, the mode opens where hasGA is false today. perf.py at ?scale=4 with the mode on: gesture p50 at or under 16.7 ms and the lens-switch ceilings unchanged.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: The plan goes from showing where the product stands to showing the verified route to the next milestone: a punch list derived from the lens manifests for any product, which roadmap and dashboard tools don't compute.

proposals.title: Turn trouble counts into a resumable inspection route
proposals.outcome: A lens reader can systematically inspect every troubled feature, hear its name and reason, open its page, and resume where they left off.
proposals.builds_on: The plan already counts trouble, highlights matching features, and opens detailed explanations. The shaped variant already contains a next-match navigation primitive.
proposals.mechanism: Ship a first slice in 3–4 days: add Inspect beside each trouble count in the adopted subtle experience. Open a native ordered list with Previous, Next, position, and inspected progress. Keep route membership fixed while reading; hold arrivals behind an explicit new-items control. Announce each selected feature and restore focus after its page closes. Build one health-versioned membership index for counts, flags, and routes, replacing membership caches keyed only by the unchanged feature array. Keep inspected status separate from measured health.
proposals.evidence: Observed: keyboard room walking only flies the camera; the dossier records silent navigation as an accessibility deviation. Trouble totals are memoized by product identity, and flag membership by feature-array identity, although live readings mutate feature health in place. That creates a concrete invalidation gap. Existing next-match and focus-return code reduce implementation scope. Consistent keyboard focus follows [W3C guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/). Faster, more complete inspection is a hypothesis; usage is unmeasured.
proposals.risk: Live changes could move the reader's place or make inspected look equivalent to resolved. Freeze route ordering, show current health independently, and invalidate semantic membership on health changes.
proposals.verify: With five bad and three watch features under an arbitrary manifest lens, reach all eight using only the keyboard; each selection exposes its name, reason, and position. Open and close a page without losing route position or focus. Feed a previously healthy feature becoming bad: the count and flag update, while the route reports one new item until accepted. Preserve the scale=4 gesture p50 budget of 16.7 ms.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Trouble becomes a review process with a clear endpoint. Its shared membership index also gives subsequent comparison and acceptance views a reliable foundation.

proposals.title: Compare two recorded states on the same drawing
proposals.outcome: A product lead can answer what changed between two chosen dates across the product, then inspect the recorded before-and-after values at each affected place.
proposals.builds_on: Blueprint already preserves spatial position during time travel and honestly distinguishes missing historical information. Stage replay and metric histories provide two usable sources of dated evidence.
proposals.mechanism: Let the reader pin baseline A and choose endpoint B on the timeline. Derive a comparison index when endpoints or source data change. At site zoom, show counts of affected features by place; closer in, add distinct marks for stage changes, numeric movements, and first observations. Keep lifecycle fill tied to B. The feature page shows both values, measurement dates, methods, and evidence. Encode the baseline in existing URL state. The first version compares recorded stages and metrics; historical health retains its unrecorded status.
proposals.evidence: Observed: weekly change summaries compare only stages, while metric rows compare against the immediately previous reading rather than a chosen review baseline. A read-only count of the shipped Kettle log found 566 events and zero lens-health events, so historical health cannot be promised from that fixture. [Figma's change comparison](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/15023193382935-Compare-changes-in-Dev-Mode) demonstrates the interaction pattern of selecting a baseline and navigating changed objects. Its value for product reviews remains a hypothesis.
proposals.risk: Sparse or incompatible measurements could imply continuity or improvement that was never observed. Show actual reading timestamps, distinguish first observations from changes, flag incompatible methods or units, and preserve unknown historical verdicts.
proposals.verify: Use three features: one changes stage and has a metric move from 120 to 180; another receives its first measurement; the third stays unchanged. Mark exactly two features, report the stage change, show the numeric movement, and label the first observation without inventing a zero baseline. Exclude future readings and unmerged branch after-readings. Endpoint changes must leave every world rectangle and the camera unchanged, and a copied URL must restore the comparison.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: The drawing becomes a spatial review document: readers can inspect a period's changes without repeatedly scrubbing and remembering separate states.

proposals.title: Project changed files onto product impact
proposals.outcome: A maintainer can paste a changed-file list and see which product features share those code contexts, their potential downstream reach, and the evidence available for reviewing them.
proposals.builds_on: The feature page already connects product places to code contexts and file paths. The model also maintains dependencies and computes transitive used-by closures.
proposals.mechanism: Add a Changed files entry to the plan inspector. Build a reverse index from context file paths to feature IDs when the structure revision changes. Match pasted repository-relative paths, distinguish context-mapped features from potential downstream dependents, and show unmatched files explicitly. Draw two outline styles over the existing geometry and aggregate counts at room and wing levels. Selecting a match explains the complete file-to-context-to-feature chain and opens its existing lens evidence. Cache the derived sets outside the frame loop.
proposals.evidence: Observed: CodeTree currently exposes this mapping only in the feature-to-files direction; blast radius already supplies the adjacent dependency operation. The shipped sample has 75 contexts but only one with file paths, so it cannot establish useful matching coverage; pilot this on a live product with populated paths. [CodeScene's architectural analysis](https://docs.enterprise.codescene.io/versions/6.6.10/guides/architectural/architectural-analyses.html) provides prior art for lifting file-level information into architectural units. Better review scoping is a hypothesis.
proposals.risk: A context can serve many features, and declared dependencies are incomplete. Label results as mapped or potentially downstream, expose provenance and mapping coverage, and identify the loaded graph revision. An unmapped path must remain visible as uncertainty.
proposals.verify: In a fixture where one changed file maps through a shared context to A and B, C depends on A, and D is unrelated, show A and B as mapped, C as potentially downstream, and leave D unmarked. Include an unmatched file in the result. Dependency cycles must terminate and deduplicate. A product without file-path coverage must explain the gap rather than report no impact.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Blueprint gains a practical code-review job using information it already carries. A file list becomes a product-level inspection scope with traceable reasoning.

proposals.title: Make acceptance conditions executable on the drawing
proposals.outcome: A product lead can define what must be demonstrated for a selected product area, then see which conditions pass, fail, or lack current evidence—and what measured changes would clear the failures.
proposals.builds_on: Manifest lenses already turn arbitrary data into explained rules, and what-clears-it verifies proposed value changes. Stable places give those conditions a persistent product context.
proposals.mechanism: Introduce named acceptance sheets over explicit feature sets, such as Checkout inspection. Readers select required lenses, field conditions, and evidence-age limits through manifest-driven controls. Save definitions as per-product browser UI metadata with a shareable definition link. Evaluate each clause on scan/map updates and at its next freshness expiry. Show required checks and evidence coverage separately; missing required inputs stay unproven. Assemble existing clearPath results into a clause-linked clearance list, retaining blocked explanations. Distinguish target previews from observed readings and manual health overrides from rule satisfaction. Fingerprint rule definitions so changed criteria require review. Public product and event schemas remain unchanged.
proposals.evidence: Observed: GA readiness is gated on the sample's specific milestone, whereas manifest rules and clearance calculations are generic. A read-only execution confirmed that quality values with two P1 bugs and 92% passing tests produce two clearance steps; applying both changes the evaluator from bad to good. That establishes solver feasibility, not user value or real-world causality. [Spotify Soundcheck](https://backstage.spotify.com/docs/plugins/soundcheck/core-concepts) demonstrates scoped checks over collected facts. The hypothesis is that spatial, cross-lens acceptance makes Blueprint useful for expressing product intent as well as inspecting status.
proposals.risk: A reassuring summary could overstate what the evidence proves. Show clause-level sources, timestamps, coverage, overrides, and unresolved conditions; name the result criteria met. Re-evaluate all clauses after actual measurements, since isolated clearance steps do not establish cross-lens causality.
proposals.verify: Create a two-feature sheet requiring quality and a custom cost lens. Two failing quality rules plus one stale cost reading must prevent success and expose both clearance steps and the stale evidence. Editing target previews must leave observed status unchanged. Fresh current-product readings satisfying every clause must pass; a regression must fail, and evidence expiry must become unproven. A good override or an unmerged branch after-reading must not satisfy a required measured clause. Rule-definition changes must surface for review.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Blueprint becomes a living acceptance drawing: people state what must be true at product places, and evidence continually supports or invalidates those conditions.

proposals.title: Walk a lens's trouble by keyboard, spoken, on a membership index that stays fresh
proposals.outcome: A lens reader using a keyboard or screen reader presses N (Shift+N goes back) to step through every feature the current lens marks bad or watch (under General, every lens's), in the plan's room-walk order. Each arrival flies the camera, highlights the tile and announces '3 of 8 · Payments › Card vault · Security bad: 2 secrets found · clears at secrets at most 0'. Enter opens the page; Esc returns to the same route position. A feature that turns bad mid-walk shows as '1 new' instead of reshuffling the route. Left/right room walks speak the room's lens sentence. Flags and 'Trouble by lens' counts update when a live reading turns a feature bad, which today they do not.
proposals.builds_on: Every lens, including code-free manifest lenses, already yields per-feature trouble with a reason, place aggregates, and verified clearPath steps. flyToFeature already highlights, the 600 ms rest already gates browser history, and the sheet already returns focus.
proposals.mechanism: (1) Replace the flags.ts TROUBLED WeakMap and the Overview kc memo with one engine-owned index, troubled features per lens, rebuilt when sim.healthV changes, where Engine.ts:426 already clears the raster and aggregate caches. layoutFlags, the counts and the route all read it. (2) N captures a route: the index for the current lens, ordered by M.L.walk room index then tile order, frozen while reading. New members go into a count until accepted; current health is shown separately from route membership. (3) The cursor uses shaped's nextMatch logic (lifted to engine/), flyToFeature(id, true) and a visually hidden polite live region. The region's text comes from one pure routeWords(E, id, lens, i, n): the hover card's place summary, the trouble reason and clearPath's first step. It replaces the text instead of appending, and only after the camera rests. (4) walk() pushes the room sentence through the same region, closing the canvas-accessibility deviation. N and Shift+N are unbound today; J/K belong to stepDecision. React reads only on discrete store changes.
proposals.evidence: Observed: restate does Object.assign(f, troubleOf(...)), changing f.trouble on the same objects, while troubled() caches by array identity, and its comment says 'the list never changes after load'. The healthV branch clears only the cache and aggLensCache, so flags miss newly troubled features on live products and in Kettle's scan sim, which shares the live path. The recorded deviation (walk() announces nothing) is the same gap P02 names, and P05's route closes it for features, not only rooms. Hypothesis: a route with an endpoint is used more than free scrubbing; usage is unmeasured.
proposals.risk: Announcement noise during flights, and readers taking 'visited' to mean 'fixed'. Mitigation: speak only after the camera rests and replace rather than queue. Keep health words live and separate from route position, and never store 'inspected' as health. Rebuilding the index costs features × lenses on a healthV change, never per frame.
proposals.verify: A node check feeds a scan snapshot that turns feature X bad under security: before, layoutFlags returns no flag for X and the Overview count is unchanged; after, X is flagged and the count rises by 1. A browser run on Kettle under one lens: N from the plan visits every bad/watch feature exactly once in M.L.walk order, the live region's text changes once per arrival, Shift+N reverses, and opening and closing a page keeps the position. A feed mid-route shows '1 new' and leaves the order unchanged. ArrowRight twice changes the region twice. A re-judge moves canvas-graph/canvas-accessibility off deviation. perf.py ?scale=4 gesture p50 stays at or under 16.7 ms.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Trouble becomes a walk with an end that anyone can take without sight or a mouse, for any lens anyone adds. It also fixes a silent bug where the plan stops flagging new trouble after the first live reading.

proposals.title: Readiness for whatever the plan has selected: verified steps, coverage and evidence age
proposals.outcome: The reader presses G on whatever they're looking at: a lasso or Mark selection, the current room or wing, a milestone if the map has one, or else the whole product. The plan dims everything else and the callout reads, for example, 'Checkout · 14 features: 9 clear every lens · 2 unproven (readings older than 30 d) · 11 steps, 4 covered by proposals that clear them, 1 falls short · 1 blocked'. Steps are numbered on existing flags, counts sit on room labels, and each step opens its lens tab at 'what clears it'. Live products without milestones, which today get no readiness view at all, get one.
proposals.builds_on: GA readiness mode (dim, frame, callout), clearPath's verified steps, the scan contract's per-proposal metric and expected delta, and the explicit feature sets the plan already makes (lasso, Mark, Find).
proposals.mechanism: Add a pure core readiness(P, scan, ids, {maxAgeDays, now}). For each feature in scope and each enabled lens it gives one verdict: clear; unproven, when the pair's newest current reading is older than maxAgeDays (after-phase pack readings never count, as today); steps from clearPath; or blocked with its reason. A cross-lens pass applies all of a feature's steps and re-reads every lens with readLens, reporting conflicts in words. Coverage per step re-runs the step's rule on now + expected_delta for proposed/approved/executing proposals, and uses after_value for done ones. Scope resolution is S.tgt, else the current place, else a milestone, else everything. Generalize S.ga to S.ready = {scope}. syncModeFilters' dimFn becomes 'in scope', setMode frames tilesBox, and the GA callout takes the readiness summary. The hash carries ready=<place or milestone id>. Criteria are the lens manifests themselves, so there is no authoring UI and no browser-only store. Evidence age is one control, defaulting from the scan cadence. Nothing recolours a node.
proposals.evidence: Observed: hasGA is false unless the map has payments-ga, and bp's own adopted live map has 21 features, none with a milestone and no milestones list. So both GA mode and a milestone-only punch list are absent on exactly the live products they should serve; P08's explicit sets fix that, and the plan already makes them (setTarget from lasso, Mark, Find). clearPath already verifies steps by applying targets and re-running the rules. Measurements carry measured_at and phase, but no code treats an old reading as weaker than a fresh one (health.ts's only 'fresh' is a manifest compile cache), so today a 90-day-old good reading reads as good. Hypothesis: on products scanned irregularly a real share of 'good' pairs would read unproven; unmeasured.
proposals.risk: A tidy summary could overstate readiness, and cross-lens fixes can conflict. Mitigation: unproven is its own count and never folds into clear; conflicts are stated, not hidden; every number links to the step and its reading date. Ship the pure readiness function and callout first; numbered flags and coverage chips come after. It is computed on discrete scope, scan or date changes only, never per frame.
proposals.verify: A check:readiness fixture of 5 features under maxAge 30 d: one clean with a fresh reading, one clean with a 45-day-old reading, one with 1 step covered by a clearing proposal, one with 2 steps where one proposal falls short, one blocked. It yields '1 of 5 clear · 1 unproven · 3 steps, 1 covered, 1 short · 1 blocked', and an after-phase reading never makes a feature clear. A cross-lens conflict fixture is reported. On a live map with no milestone, G over a room opens the mode, where today the key does nothing. perf.py ?scale=4 with the mode on: gesture p50 at or under 16.7 ms and lens-switch ceilings unchanged.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Any part of any product, picked the way the plan already picks things, gets a verified, evidence-dated route to done from the lens manifests alone. It also says honestly what is stale instead of calling it good.

proposals.title: Distinguish measurement regressions from changed lens criteria
proposals.outcome: A reviewer can compare two dates and determine whether a changed rule assessment follows from changed measurements, changed criteria, both, or insufficient comparable evidence.
proposals.builds_on: Blueprint preserves spatial position, retains dated metric readings, and evaluates manifest rules deterministically; its existing presenter already distinguishes recorded facts from unavailable historical health.
proposals.mechanism: When the reader pins baseline A, retain the selected lens's current rule and field definitions as review metadata, explicitly labelled criteria pinned today rather than historical criteria. Compare recorded inputs at A and endpoint B under that same definition. If the installed manifest subsequently changes, additionally evaluate both input sets under the new definition, presenting measurement movement and criteria movement as separate comparisons. Construct fresh evaluation facets from dated readings and replayed stage only; never copy current overrides, facet applicability, other facet values, or current KPIs into the past. Rule applicability is computed only when its required inputs are recorded. Missing inputs, incompatible units or methods, and excessive reading age remain explicit gaps. Show affected-place counts and an inspectable feature list over unchanged geometry, with each verdict linked to its complete input vector and actual measurement dates. Cache results on endpoint, measurement-table, and criteria changes outside the frame loop; keep ordinary historical health labelled unrecorded.
proposals.evidence: Observed: metricHistory excludes branch after-readings and orders readings by measurement time; evaluateLens exposes the deciding rule and bound values. A read-only fixture produced bad from a dated value of 120 against a limit of 100, but good when a current override was copied into that facet, demonstrating why replay needs fresh inputs. The crossed comparisons require deterministic evaluations, not a causal model. Whether reviewers frequently need criteria-versus-measurement attribution remains a hypothesis.
proposals.risk: Readers could mistake projected rule assessments for recorded historical health or treat asynchronous observations as simultaneous measurements; label projections separately, expose every source timestamp, enforce comparability and age checks, and report mixed changes without claiming a unique cause.
proposals.verify: With A=80 and B=120 under a pinned bad-above-100 rule, report a measurement regression. Changing the rule to bad-above-70 must separately show a criteria regression at A. Unchanged readings with a tightened threshold must produce only a criteria change. A current good override must not alter either historical projection; branch after-readings and future readings must be excluded. Missing required fields or incompatible methods must yield unknown. Endpoint changes must preserve every world rectangle and the camera, and scale=4 gesture p50 must remain at or below 16.7 ms.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: The drawing explains why an assessment changed across a review period, including changes to the measuring stick itself. It advances historical replay without presenting reconstructed judgments as recorded facts.

proposals.title: Track milestone clearance from proposed fixes to observed proof
proposals.outcome: A product lead can inspect any milestone and distinguish requirements that lack evidence, fixes that only project success, results demonstrated on a branch, and conditions actually satisfied by current product measurements.
proposals.builds_on: Generic milestone membership already exists, clearPath proposes verified local changes, proposals identify related metrics, and measurement provenance already distinguishes branch evidence from product readings.
proposals.mechanism: Create a milestone acceptance sheet with explicit required stages, lenses or field conditions, and evidence-age limits, stored as per-product UI metadata with a criteria fingerprint. Derive one requirement ledger consumed by the plan counts, feature page, and inspection list. For each requirement, retain observed pass/fail/unproven separately from proposal coverage: unassigned, projected to satisfy, insufficient, or demonstrated on branch. Match proposals by base feature, lens and metric; retain missing-metric proposals as unlinked. Treat latest-value-plus-delta as an explicitly rebased projection and never add independent proposal deltas automatically. Use clearPath only to generate candidate targets, then re-evaluate the complete requested conditions; returning to a watch default does not satisfy a good requirement. A done item or after_value supplies branch evidence only. Current-product satisfaction requires fresh eligible readings and complete required inputs, with provenance shown and no automatic claim that a proposal caused the improvement. Generalize the existing milestone framing beyond payments-ga, expose separate failure and evidence-gap counts, and reopen observed failures on regression or evidence expiry. No new execution workflow or public schema is required.
proposals.evidence: Observed: milestones and feature membership are generic, but the UI gate checks the sample milestone ID. Proposal statuses include done, accepted and released, while isCurrent excludes every phase=after measurement. Read-only fixtures confirmed both that absent inputs can produce an empty clearance list and that clearPath can successfully return targets whose resulting health is watch. The proposed ledger addresses those demonstrated gaps; improved milestone decisions remain a hypothesis.
proposals.risk: A summary could imply shipment readiness or verified causality beyond its criteria; name the result criteria met, display required scope and evidence coverage, keep forecasts and branch demonstrations separate from observed status, and surface criteria changes for review.
proposals.verify: Use a live map with a milestone other than payments-ga and a latency requirement of at most 400. A current reading of 420 with a proposed delta of -30 must remain observed fail with projected coverage. Marking the proposal done with branch after_value=390 must still leave observed fail. A fresh eligible product reading of 390 must pass; a later 430 reading must fail again. Missing or expired evidence must become unproven, and a good override must not satisfy a required measured condition. A clearance path ending at watch must not satisfy a good requirement. Counts and inspection rows must agree after each scan delta, with scale=4 gesture p50 at or below 16.7 ms.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Milestone planning gains a continuous chain from requirements through intended fixes to observed evidence. The plan can show how well work covers the remaining requirements without confusing completed work with demonstrated product quality.

ratings.why: The invalidation gap is real: flags.ts:43-48 caches troubled features in a WeakMap keyed on the never-replaced P.features array, restate (live-health.ts:28-30) mutates f.trouble in place, Engine.ts:426 never clears it, and plan.tsx:155-159 memoizes counts on [M.P], so a feature a scan turns bad gets no flag or count; nextMatch exists only in the shaped legend, and the 'inspected' state has no stated home.

Claims check out (changes.ts:14-23 diffs adjacent weeks' stages only, LensTab's 'was' is the previous reading, kettle.events.jsonl has 566 events and 0 lens-health), but it gives up health, the question a history reader most brings, and its numeric side is empty on the one-reading sample, so it adds little over weekChanges except a chosen span.

CodeTree is feature-to-files only, as claimed, and although Kettle has 1 of 75 contexts with paths, bp's own live map has paths on 29 of 29 contexts at one feature each, so matching would be precise; but pasting a list is clumsy input, and the job is a maintainer's code review rather than one of the dossier's named readers.

Anchors hold (GA is tied to payments-ga at Engine.ts:777-779; clearPath and readLens are generic), and evidence age is a real gap (health.ts's only 'fresh' is a manifest compile cache), but most of the L effort is an authoring UI for conditions nobody has asked to write, stored per browser where Personas and VR cannot read them.

timeview.ts:81-86 and live.ts:25-34 confirm the replay opportunity, but health.ts:185-193 also reads facet applicability and overrides, so checking rule-field coverage alone cannot prevent current metadata from leaking into historical verdicts.

Engine.ts:695-703 confirms silent walking and :1035-1048 supplies a discrete arrival hook, making announcements excellent value, although rail/wide/shell.tsx:27-45,97-107 already provides roving feature navigation and capped proxies cannot establish complete accessibility.

LensPanel.tsx:138-151 and Queue.tsx:16-22 support useful proposal coverage, but scan/types.ts:60-65 and scan/derive.ts:23-27 explicitly separate branch after-readings from product state, making the proposed delivered-clearance verdict unjustified.

Engine.ts:778 confirms the milestone gate depends on milestone presence rather than product liveness, while clear.ts:84-119 and read-only fixtures show that missing inputs can yield no steps and verified clearance can end at watch, leaving the expensive all-lens readiness claim insufficiently supported.
